para.text: has described global zooming meaning that the zoom factors for all Y-axes are the same. However also differential zooming can occur where the zooming factors may be different for each Y-axis.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

para.text: Differential zooming may occur accidentally when an Y-axis has endfitting set (see
). In that case the actual axis ends may be adjusted and therefore can differ from the original settings. This can cause (slightly) different zooming factors for different Y-axes.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: Different zooming however can also be performed by using
. This commands sets the zooming factors for an individual axis (either X or Y). The command does not redraw the graph automatically, you have to do that yourself.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: Another way to obtain differential zooming is by an adapted mouse operation as follows.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: If you perform zooming with the mouse as described on the previous page the zooming is set to the X-axis and all Y-axes (global zooming).

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: However if you hit any of the function keys F1-F4 during the operation (don’t forget to use
), differential zooming is automatically selected and only the Y-axes of which the corresponding function key was hit (1-4) will be affected (that means the X-axis will always remain the same).

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: You can momentarily release the Control key to hit the function keys, as long as the Control key is pressed again when you release the mouse button.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: Please note that differential zooming only works correctly in the way described above. Many other zooming operations like zooming with the keyboard use the global settings only (= the main of all individual Y settings). Zooming with the mouse is the only way that truly uses the individual actual zoom settings.
